speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your history of recurrent urinary tract infections and current flank pain with blood, could you tell me if you have noticed any fever, chills, or nausea, and have you ever had a stone detected in your kidney or ureter?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture.
REQUEST TEST: Renal Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance - Reddish; WBC - 10-20 /HPF; RBC - Too numerous to count; Nitrites - Negative; Leukocyte_Esterase - Positive. Renal Ultrasound: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The urinalysis shows significant blood and white blood cells with positive leukocyte esterase but negative nitrites, suggesting an inflammatory or infectious process, and your ultrasound is normal. Have you noticed any clots in your urine, and do you experience painless bleeding or painless weight loss?

REQUEST TEST: CT KUB (Computed Tomography of Kidneys, Ureters, and Bladder).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT KUB: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction noted.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney.

The CT KUB confirms multiple cysts in the medullary collecting ducts, which explains your recurrent hematuria and flank pain in the context of your history of urinary tract infections. I have reached my limit of questions and tests.
